trace.title: Service identity
trace.detail:
## Understand the idea

Datadog combines observability capabilities such as infrastructure monitoring, APM, logs, and monitors. Choose the signals needed for a concrete investigation.

Installing an agent alone does not make every request/job trace connected.

Use stable service, environment, and version tags. Instrument the relevant Rails/client/job libraries with versions supported by your runtime.

Current datadog gem setup differs from legacy ddtrace setups; a Rails 4.2/Ruby 2.7 application needs a verified compatibility choice.

Setup path: choose supported tracer/agent versions, configure a training service identity and agent path, instrument a request and worker, correlate logs safely, define a useful monitor/runbook, and verify with a synthetic slow dependency.

Review sampling, sensitive fields, ingestion, retention, and billing dimensions.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
User-visible latency spike → service latency/error metrics → slow trace → SQL or provider span → correlated safe logs → hypothesis → controlled repair → monitor recovery.

Async boundaries need explicit context propagation/linking rather than assuming one synchronous stack.

An absent trace can mean sampling or missing instrumentation, not proof the request never ran.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail:
Unbounded tags and full payload capture can create cost/privacy problems. A monitor without a clear action becomes noise.

Trace instrumentation can be misconfigured even when infrastructure metrics arrive.
